metaDescription: Hold coalbed methane or mineral interests near Nauvoo, AL in Walker County? Get a courthouse-verified offer from a patient, direct buyer, no pressure.
heroLead: Nauvoo sits deep in Walker County coal country, where the same Mary Lee and Blue Creek coal seams that were mined underground for a century were later drilled a second time for the methane trapped inside them.
intro: Walker County produced more coal than almost anywhere else in Alabama, and Nauvoo's rural acreage was part of that story for generations before coalbed methane became its own business in the 1980s and 1990s. That second wave of leasing often ran through a different chain of ownership than the original coal rights, and it's not unusual for a family here to hold a mineral interest without a clear sense of whether it's tied to old coal royalties, an active CBM unit, or both at once.

sections.heading: Two Layers of History Under the Same Ground
paragraphs: The coal companies that worked this part of Walker County decades ago frequently kept the coal but sold or leased the surface, and when CBM operators came through later, they leased the gas separately from whoever held it at the time. A single tract near Nauvoo can carry coal rights, gas rights, and surface ownership held by three different parties — we sort out which layer your family actually owns before we make an offer.

sections.heading: What a Jasper Courthouse Search Turns Up
paragraphs: The Walker County Courthouse in Jasper holds the deed and probate records we pull to trace a Nauvoo-area interest back to its origin, and for anything touching an active CBM unit we also check the state's pooling and unitization filings. That combination usually answers the ownership question within a few days once we have the legal description.

faqs.question: How do we know if our interest is coal, gas, or both?
faqs.answer: That comes down to what the original deed reserved and what's been leased since. We check the Walker County record and tell you plainly what your family actually holds.

faqs.question: Our royalty checks stopped years ago. Is the interest still worth anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly — a well can be shut in or the unit reorganized without the underlying mineral interest losing value. We look at the unit's current status before pricing it.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the original coal company doesn't exist anymore?
faqs.answer: No, it just means we trace who the interest sold or passed to over the years. That research is ours to do, not yours.

faqs.question: Our family has owned this ground near Nauvoo since before the CBM boom. Does that history help or hurt us?
faqs.answer: It helps. A long, documented chain of ownership makes title easier to confirm, which usually means a faster path to closing once we've reviewed the record.
